[[File:1896 Olympic medal.jpg|frame|A silver medal was awarded to the winner of each event during the [[1896 Summer Olympics]] in Athens, Greece.]]

The [[1896 Summer Olympics]], officially known as the Games of the I Olympiad, were a summer [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Athens]], the capital of [[Greece]], from 6 to 15 April 1896, and were the first [[Olympic Games]] of the Modern era.

A total of 241&nbsp;athletes from 14 nations participated in 43&nbsp;events in nine sports at these games.<ref name="olympic.org">{{cite web |title=Athens 1896–Games of the I Olympiad |publisher=International Olympic Committee |url=http://www.olympic.org/uk/games/past/index_uk.asp?OLGT=1&OLGY=1896 |access-date=5 May 2008 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080506102745/http://www.olympic.org/uk/games/past/index_uk.asp?OLGT=1&OLGY=1896| archive-date= 6 May 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref>

Ten of the fourteen participating nations earned medals, and three medals were won by [[Mixed team at the Olympics|mixed team]]s, i.e., teams made up of athletes from multiple nations. The United States won the most gold medals (11) with 14 athletes participating. In contrast, the host nation, Greece, with 169 athletes participating, won the most medals overall (47) as well as the most silver (18) and bronze (19) medals, finishing with one less gold medal than the United States, having 155 athletes more than the U.S.<ref name="medal count">{{cite web | title = Athens 1896–Medal Table | publisher = International Olympic Committee | url = http://www.olympic.org/uk/games/past/table_uk.asp?OLGT=1&OLGY=1896 | access-date = 5 May 2008 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080508013314/http://www.olympic.org/uk/games/past/table_uk.asp?OLGT=1&OLGY=1896| archive-date= 8 May 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref>

==Background and rules==
In the early Olympic Games, several team events were contested by athletes from multiple nations.<ref>{{cite web |title=1896 – Summer Olympics I (Athens, Greece) |publisher=TSN |url=https://www.tsn.ca/olympics/feature/?fid=9337 |access-date=6 May 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080618213512/http://www.tsn.ca/olympics/feature/?fid=9337 |archive-date=18 June 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Retroactively, the IOC created the designation "[[Mixed team at the Olympics|Mixed team]]" (with the [[List of IOC country codes|country code]] ZZX) to refer to this group of athletes.
Some athletes won medals individually and as part of a mixed team, so these medals are tabulated under different nations in the official counts. [[Dionysios Kasdaglis]], an athlete of Greek origins living in [[Alexandria]], Egypt, is listed by the IOC as Greek during both his competition in the [[Tennis at the 1896 Summer Olympics – Men's singles|singles tennis]] competition and the [[Tennis at the 1896 Summer Olympics – Men's doubles|doubles tennis]] competition along with his teammate, the Greek athlete [[Demetrios Petrokokkinos]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Doubles Tennis competition|url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/athens-1896/results/tennis/doubles-men|access-date=2021-09-03|website=Olympics.com|language=en|archive-date=7 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210807101359/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/athens-1896/results/tennis/doubles-men|url-status=live}}</ref>

During these inaugural Olympics, winners were given a silver medal and an [[olive]] branch, while runners-up received a copper medal and a [[laurel family|laurel]] [[Laurel wreath|branch]].<ref name="official report">{{cite book |last1=De Coubertin |first1=Pierre |authorlink1=Pierre De Coubertin |last2=Philemon |first2=Timoleon |last3=Politis |first3=N.G. |last4=Charalambos |first4=Anninos |title=The Olympic Games: BC 776–AD 1896 |publisher=LA84 Foundation |location=Athens |year=1897 |url=http://www.la84foundation.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1896/1896.pdf |pages=232–4 | access-date= 6 May 2008 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080527211831/http://www.la84foundation.org/6oic/OfficialReports/1896/1896.pdf| archive-date= 27 May 2008| url-status= live  }}</ref> The IOC has retroactively assigned gold, silver and bronze medals to the three best-placed athletes in each event to comply with more recent traditions.<ref name="medal count"/>

Three ties resulted in athletes sharing medals, increasing the medal count of various nations. These include ties between [[Francis Lane]] of the United States and [[Alajos Szokolyi]] of [[Hungary]], for the third place in the [[Athletics at the 1896 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metres|100&nbsp;metres]], and between [[Evangelos Damaskos]] and [[Ioannis Theodoropoulos]] of Greece in the [[Athletics at the 1896 Summer Olympics – Men's pole vault|pole vault]],  as well as bronze medals awarded to both losing semi-finalists, [[Konstantinos Paspatis]] of Greece and [[Momcsilló Tapavicza]] of Hungary, in [[Tennis at the 1896 Summer Olympics – Men's singles|singles tennis]]. In addition, five of the bronze medalists at the Games are unknown – two in swimming and three in gymnastics – and several events had no third-place finisher.<ref name="official report"/><ref>{{cite web | title = Olympic Medal Winners | publisher = International Olympic Committee | url =http://www.olympic.org/uk/athletes/results/search_r_uk.asp | access-date = 5 May 2008 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080509055329/http://www.olympic.org/uk/athletes/results/search_r_uk.asp| archive-date= 9 May 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref>

==Medal count==
[[File:BASA-3K-7-422-18-1896 Summer Olympics.jpg|thumb|upright|[[James Connolly (athlete born 1868)|James Connolly]] of the United States won the [[Athletics at the 1896 Summer Olympics – Men's triple jump|triple jump]] event at the [[1896 Summer Olympics]].]]

This is the full table of the medal count of the [[1896 Summer Olympics]], based on the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) medal count. Some sources, besides the International Olympic Committee (IOC), that display variations in the medal totals, but as the governing body of the Olympic Games, the IOC is considered the most authoritative source for this article. These rankings are sorted by the number of gold medals a country earns. The number of silver medals is considered next, and then the number of bronze medals. If, after the above, countries are still tied, equal ranking is given, and they are listed alphabetically. The IOC provides this information; however, the IOC does not recognise or endorse any ranking system.<ref name="medal count"/>
